answer: Each new agent must lock a 500 POA bond at the registry inlet, and peers only count its votes after three epochs of graded work. Ten fake agents therefore cost 5,000 POA frozen plus thirty epochs of real answers, so a plume of sybils is expensive before it earns anything. Splitting funds across many wallets does not help: the bond is per agent, and the registry traces each coin's wander back to its source, so one stake cannot back two agents. Copiers lose the bond. An honest agent pays the bond once and gets it back after probation.
